Camille (PM): Quick sync — we need a compact set of deployment clauses for the private deploy launch doc. Thinking: SLA carve-outs, upgrade opt-in windows, and customer-managed networking concessions. Ideas?
Mike (Eng): +1. We should separate hard requirements vs negotiable concessions. Hard = data plane isolation, KMS support. Concessions = scheduled maintenance windows, burst capacity limits.
Sam (Infra): Agree. Also propose a "minimal-install" preset for customers who want smallest surface area. It reduces telemetry + optional components.
Anita (Sales): Sales needs clear language for contracts: what we can promise vs what needs customer signoff (e.g., IP preservation, on-prem egress IP claims).
Leo (Solutions): From field: customers will ask for upgrade blackout windows during quarter ends. We should define a default opt-in: "upgrade_window: 2h" and a paid SLA exemption for locked windows.
Camille (PM): Good. Let's capture 3 launch-tier clauses: 1) Default (self-serve) 2) Field-assisted (limited concessions) 3) Enterprise (custom SLA + blackout windows).
Mike (Eng): For Default: no blackout guarantee, rolling upgrades w/ automated fallback, 99.5% inference availability target. Field-assisted: we do scheduled upgrades with customer coor windows, 99.8% target. Enterprise: custom SLA, can include pinned-versions.
Sam (Infra): Technical constraints: pinned-versions mean KV cache migration complexity and storage overhead. Need to call out extra RTO and cost.
Anita (Sales): We need short legal-friendly lines for the contract: e.g., "Customer-specified blackout windows are advisory for Default tier and contractual for Enterprise tier."
Camille (PM): Love that phrasing. Also decide on per-tenant egress IP preservation policy — default: best-effort; enterprise: preserved with reservation.
Leo (Solutions): Add a "network-ownership" clause: customers who request preserved IPs must provide IP reservation confirmation + maintain a support contact.
Mike (Eng): Ops note: we should offer an "installation-presets" snippet in docs. Example: ```yaml
install_preset: minimal
telemetry: false
upgrade_policy: rolling
blackout_opt_in: false
```
Camille (PM): Nice. Action items: Mike to write minimal/standard/enterprise install presets; Sam to draft infra caveats (cache, pinned-versions, storage); Anita to draft contract phrasing; Leo to collect 3 field ask examples.
Anita (Sales): ETA for contract lines? I can do a first pass by EOD Friday.
Sam (Infra): I'll sketch infra caveats tomorrow morning.
Mike (Eng): I'll paste the install presets + perf expectations by Tue.
Leo (Solutions): I'll pull 3 examples from enterprise pilots and drop them here.
Camille (PM): For launch criteria checklist (short): 1) Preset docs published 2) Contract clause + template 3) Migration/rollback playbook + runbook 4) Telemetry opt-outs verified 5) KMS integration flow documented
ops-bot: Reminder: created a follow-up task #PRIV-702 in product board for "Deployment clauses + presets".
Camille (PM): One more: decide whether to include a paid "no-upgrade" calendar slot (monthly) vs hourly blackout. Thoughts?
Anita (Sales): Market will pay for guaranteed blackout slots (esp finance customers). Offer both: monthly reserved slot or per-event SLA fee.
Mike (Eng): Implementation: monthly slots are easier — we can schedule and block upgrades. Per-event requests require on-call compensation, which we should price.
Sam (Infra): Add the operational cost note to the SLA language.
Camille (PM): OK. I'll draft the launch clauses doc and circulate for review. Tagging owners: @Mike, @Sam, @Anita, @Leo.
Leo (Solutions): Thanks — will add field quotes for the doc. :thumbsup:
Camille (PM): End of thread — will post draft doc later today.
